title: Edge of the Woods Outfitters
specs: Take as much time as you like to drift down this stretch of river to swim, fish and picnic.
All boats must be returned by 6PM All day trips depart from our Delaware Water Gap Location.
Ages 3 and up, all ability levels welcome.
There is no potable water and food must be hung to keep the opportunistic critters like raccoons, opossums, and sometimes black bear away at night.
After a brief safety orientation, and life jacket fitting, you will be shuttled to Kittatinny Point to start the trip.
All coolers must be personal sized.
Alcohol is allowed but strongly discouraged.
Minimum age for tubing is 12 years old.
What’s Included: Free Parking at our location Life Jacket Transportation to and from the river Key Check Access to our facilities at the beginning and end of the trip.

services.name: Pedal and Paddle Package
services.desc: Want to make a splash you and your family will remember forever? This package combines our famous 5 Bridges Bike Tour with a Delaware River Trip for an unbeatable price. This great outdoor adventure begins with a leisurely float down the Delaware with plenty of time for swimming, fishing, and picnicking. The best way to experience the scenic beauty of the Delaware Water Gap National Park. Swap your bike for a boat, or use your biking voucher a different day to take this self guided bike tour. The easy, traffic free trail wanders along the river banks and through spectacular scenery along the river. Ages 3 and up, all ability levels welcome. Please note, this is a package price for 2

services.name: Overnight Canoe Camping
services.desc: About: Overnight canoe camping is a great way to experience and take in the beauty of the park. These trips can be leisurely floats or more intense paddle days depending on the section of river you choose. All offering amazing views, small sets of class 1 rapids, wildlife sightings and pristine riverfront camping. Edge of the Woods Outfitters will help you choose the right length trip for your getaway. The National Park Service maintains dozens of free primitive camp sites, available on a first come, first serve basis.
